slides.title: 9.2.1 Performing Depth-First Traversals
keyPoints: Preorder visits the node before its children, which is useful for parent-first listing or propagating inherited.

slides.narration: In Book III, Chapter 9, treat 9.2.1 Performing Depth-First Traversals as an algorithmic claim. Preorder visits the node before its children, which is useful for parent-first listing or propagating inherited context. Postorder visits children before the node, which is useful for bottom-up aggregation or releasing dependent work. The recursive implementations process each node once, giving linear traversal work in the number of nodes. Auxiliary call-stack depth is proportional to tree height, while the returned output vector itself contains one value per node. A very deep untrusted hierarchy can exceed call-stack limits; an explicit stack or bounded-depth ingestion policy is needed for that broader domain.
